distinguishing_features: Use of Rayleigh wave propagation analysis for micro-crack detection
Optimization for railway rail curve gauge corners
Real-time sensor network with spacing based on Rayleigh wavelength
Detection threshold derived from Rayleigh wave scattering physics
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Providing real-time, continuous monitoring of subsurface micro-crack initiation in railway rails at high-stress curve locations without manual intervention.
parsed.viable_reason: The solution uses existing rail-mounted vibration sensors and data acquisition infrastructure, with physically sound calculations for wave velocity and detection thresholds derived from stated material properties and historical data.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The specific application of Rayleigh wave analysis to detect micro-crack nucleation in rails, including wavelength-based sensor spacing and scattering thresholds, is not an obvious adaptation of the gear-based vibration phase shift and demodulation approach in prior art 1.
